# BUNDAR CT/X labeled replay v1

`ct_x_v1.json` contains 19 manually labeled synthetic cases (22 accepted posts and one intentionally rejected future post). It is not collected from X and does not measure trading performance. Addresses/accounts are synthetic. Gold labels are authored in the fixture, not generated by parser output. Reproduce the report with:

```powershell
$env:PYTHONPATH = 'src'
python -m meme_coin_radar.ct_replay tests/fixtures/ct_x_v1.json --output CT_X_REPLAY_REPORT.json
```

Cases 01–15 cover direct contract, unique ticker, ticker collision, external catalyst without coin, early distinct accounts, late receipt, duplicate promotion, competition, irrelevant text, repost, quote, reply, missing fields, future leakage and false association. Cases 16–19 cover token-name aliases, unregistered subjects, negated association and an unresolved address.

Early independent propagation is represented as two distinct observed account IDs; independence remains unknown. Late/chasing propagation is represented by posting/receipt delay, not a judgment of a trader. Original-catalyst labels are candidate descriptions based on literal subject matches and no observed references; originality and causal effect are unverified. Negated subject/contract association still contains an objectively observed address mention; it never produces capture/identity/hypothesis evidence.

Exact case match includes relationship, descriptive class, subjects, possible catalyst marker, direct coin IDs and specified count expectations. The expected future rejection counts as a successful guard. Identity precision/recall/accuracy evaluate **DIRECT_CONTRACT_REFERENCE for the supplied target** only; relationship metrics are also reported per label. Unknown classifications and ambiguous relationships are counted separately and can overlap. Coverage is the proportion of supplied cases attempted, not X population coverage. Unsupported-inference checks detect missing lineage or an exact-contract result without a resolved contract ID; they do not certify semantic truth.

A perfect result on this small, rule-focused dataset establishes implementation conformance only. Real-X accuracy/recall, unseen ticker collisions and source coverage remain unmeasured. Build a separately labeled held-out real-response dataset before relying on live parser results. Retain failures and unknowns.
